docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Traditional voice assistants suffer from 2-3s latency due to sequential processing, creating unnatural conversations. Commercial solutions require expensive cloud APIs.

Key challenges: - Latency compounds across STT → LLM → TTS pipeline - Fixed silence thresholds cause premature interruptions or awkward delays - Audio artifacts at chunk boundaries - Whisper hallucinates on low-signal audio - GPU memory constraints with multiple large models

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Built an end-to-end conversational voice AI achieving human-like interactions with sub-1.5s latency, entirely self-hosted.

Core Pipeline:

Component Model Latency VRAM VAD Silero + Prosodic Turn Detection ~30ms CPU STT Whisper Large-v3-Turbo ~150ms ~3GB LLM Llama 3.2 3B (4-bit NF4) ~200ms ~7GB TTS CSM-1B Streaming ~320ms ~5GB

Key Technical Decisions:

  1. Prosodic Turn Detection — Goes beyond silence detection. Analyzes pitch contour (falling = complete), energy decay, speaking rate slowdown, and final pause. State machine tracks SILENCE → SPEAKING → JUST_STARTED → JUST_ENDED.

  2. CSM-1B Streaming TTS — Transformer backbone with KV-cache optimization. Mimi codec with 32 codebooks at 12.5Hz. First chunk sent after 4 frames (~320ms). Equal-power crossfading eliminates artifacts.

  3. Conversation Context Preservation — Audio context from previous turns enables prosodic continuity, voice consistency, emotional tone matching, and natural rhythm.

  4. Multiple Pipeline Modes:

  5. StreamingPipeline: True streaming (~600ms first audio)
  6. SmartPipeline: Filler + overlap (~50ms perceived)

  7. SeamlessPipeline: High-quality (~1.5s)

  8. Barge-in Handling — VAD runs during playback. Detects user speech >200ms, cancels TTS generation, aborts audio callback, processes interruption immediately.

  9. Echo Cancellation — 300ms cooldown after Ava stops speaking + energy-based filtering prevents responding to own voice.

Turn Detection Algorithm: 

Score = (0.35 × Pitch_Falling) +
        (0.25 × Energy_Decay) +
        (0.20 × Speaking_Rate_Slowdown) +
        (0.20 × Final_Pause)

If Score ≥ 0.55 → Turn Complete

TTS Optimizations: - KV-cache patching (removed .item() CPU-GPU sync bottlenecks) - TF32 acceleration for Ampere+ GPUs - cuDNN dynamic kernel selection - Chunk crossfading for seamless playback

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• <1.5s end-to-end latency (competitive with commercial ~465-510ms)
  • ~320ms time to first audio chunk
  • 93% turn detection accuracy
  • Seamless audio with no clicks or artifacts
  • Self-hosted — no cloud API dependencies
  • Fits in 24GB VRAM with ~7GB headroom

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: HuggingFace abstracts tokenization and attention. To truly understand LLMs, I needed to build from scratch—no pre-built components.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Complete text classification pipeline implementing every component.

What I built:

  • BPE Tokenizer — Merge most frequent pairs iteratively to build vocabulary. Handles OOV via subword decomposition.
  • Positional Encoding — Sinusoidal embeddings for token order (attention is permutation-invariant)
  • Multi-Head Attention — Q, K, V projections with scaled dot-product
  • Feed Forward — Position-wise dense layers with GELU
  • Training Loop — LR warmup, gradient clipping, early stopping

docs.title: What I learned
docs.text:
• Vocabulary size affects capacity/generalization tradeoff
  • Attention patterns emerge from training
  • Positional encoding interaction with attention
  • Initialization and normalization matter

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• 92% accuracy on AG News 4-class classification
  • Validated understanding of transformer internals
  • Foundation for larger model work

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
HeyMaya needed conversational AI to handle HR workflows on WhatsApp—candidate screening, recruiter queries, and client management. Requirements:

  • Multi-turn conversations with context retention
  • Domain expertise in HR terminology
  • Enterprise-scale reliability (1000+ concurrent users)
  • Cost-effective (GPT-4 too expensive at volume)

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B using QLoRA on 50K+ HR conversations.

Key decisions:

  • QLoRA — 4-bit quantization + LoRA enabled training on single A100 while maintaining quality
  • Entity Memory — Custom context layer tracks user state across sessions without context window limits
  • vLLM — PagedAttention for efficient KV-cache, dynamic batching for throughput
  • Infrastructure — SageMaker endpoints with auto-scaling, PostgreSQL persistence, Redis caching

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Handles 1,000+ concurrent conversations at peak
  • 97% intent accuracy on held-out test data
  • 40% cost reduction vs GPT-4 with better domain performance
  • 200ms P95 latency end-to-end

Stack: Llama 3.1 8B · QLoRA · vLLM · AWS SageMaker · PostgreSQL · Redis

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Demucs/Spleeter fail on Indian classical music:

  • Microtones — Ragas use ornamentations not in Western scales
  • Frequency overlap — Tabla, sitar, vocals share spectral regions
  • Rhythm — Tala cycles ≠ 4/4 time signatures

Tested Demucs: vocals bled, tabla smeared, sitar cut off.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Custom U-Net trained specifically on Indian classical.

Key decisions:

  • 4096-point STFT — Fine frequency resolution for microtonal detection
  • Self-attention bottleneck — Models long-range dependencies (drone + melody)
  • Multi-task decoders — Shared encoder, specialized heads per instrument
  • Raga-aware augmentation — Pitch shift within scale constraints

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text: Curated 100+ hours with manual stem annotations: - Hindustani vocals (khayal, thumri) - Sitar-tabla duets - Multiple gharanas for generalization

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• +53% SDR over Demucs baseline
  • Clean tabla transients
  • Preserved sitar sustain
  • Minimal vocal bleed

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: PyTorch handles backprop automatically. To understand neural networks, I needed to implement gradient computation myself—no autograd.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
MLP from scratch with manual forward/backward passes.

What I built:

  • Forward Propagation — Matrix multiplications, ReLU, softmax
  • Backpropagation — Derived and implemented gradients per layer type
  • Adam Optimizer — Momentum + adaptive learning rates
  • Dropout — Inverted dropout with proper train/test scaling

docs.title: What I learned
docs.text:
• Vanishing gradients — Why sigmoid fails deep, how ReLU helps
  • Learning rate — Too high = divergence, too low = slow convergence
  • Initialization — Xavier/He matter for deep networks
  • Batch norm — Why normalizing activations stabilizes training

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• 98% accuracy validates correct implementation
  • Deep understanding of gradient flow
  • Foundation for debugging training issues

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: LLMs hallucinate when answering fact-based questions. They cannot cite sources and don't adapt to new data. Researchers need accurate, grounded answers with proper citations.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
Built a RAG backend that grounds LLM responses in real arXiv papers, eliminating hallucinations through source citations.

How it works:

  1. User submits question via FastAPI /ask endpoint
  2. Question embedded using sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
  3. FAISS similarity search retrieves top-k relevant papers
  4. Papers' abstracts and titles form the context
  5. AWS Bedrock generates answer grounded in retrieved content
  6. Returns answer + source paper citations

Key components:

  • FastAPI Backend — Clean REST endpoint accepting questions, returning structured responses
  • FAISS Vector Store — L2 distance search over paper embeddings
  • Sentence Transformers — all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for semantic similarity
  • AWS Bedrock — LLM generation with context injection
  • arXiv Integration — Fetches papers with metadata and abstracts

docs.title: Technical Details
docs.text:
Vector search: 

query_embedding = model.encode([query])
distances, indices = index.search(query_embedding, top_k=3)
return [papers[i] for i in indices]

Generation prompt: 

Answer concisely and factually.
Use only the provided papers.

Question: {query}
Papers: {retrieved_abstracts}

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Eliminates hallucinations through source grounding
  • Every answer backed by citable arXiv papers
  • Clean separation of retrieval and generation
  • Stateless, scalable backend architecture
